transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, I just can't seem to shut my brain off lately. It's... it's getting out of hand. I'll have one small thing happen at work—like a client doesn't email back right away—and suddenly I'm just spiraling. I start thinking I'm going to lose the contract, and then... then I'm worrying about how I'll make my divorce payments, and... I just convince myself I'm never going to get back to a real leadership role. It just doesn't stop.
Do these anxious thoughts tend to happen in just one area of your life, like work, or do they pop up in different areas, like relationships or personal health as well?

It's... well, it jumps around. Not just work. I'll be thinking about the contract work, and then it's... the mortgage payments. Or... I don't know, just worrying about the Bethesda tech circles... if people around there think I'm damaged goods now. It's just... a delayed email from a recruiter is enough to make me think my whole career is closing down. So... yeah. It's different things.
Do you notice any physical symptoms when these worries come up, like restlessness, muscle tension, or trouble sleeping?

Yeah... I guess so. I just feel... wound up, mostly. Like, all day. My shoulders get really tight, like they're just locked in place... like I'm bracing for something bad to happen. And I can't really sit still. I end up pacing around the house a lot, or... bouncing my leg when I'm on calls. Even when it's just a normal day and nothing's going on.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends?
No... I wouldn't say that. I don't really feel hopeless. Just... tired from all the thinking, I guess. I still do things when I can. It's just the worrying that's the issue.
